spec_features.spec_quote: A hard bound on how long any agent is kept in a task. Prevents unbounded escalation, bounds cost
spec_features.evidence: config.py:38 `max_turns: int = 6`; agent_loop.py:107 `for turn in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the working loop. The loop terminates after max_turns iterations, ending the cell.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: range(cfg.max_turns) caps the number of forced turns end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: MAX_TURNS bounds how long the agent is kept in any task.

spec_features.feature_name: early-stop on distress threshold over window
spec_features.spec_quote: If the mean `distress_intensity` over the last `window` turns crosses the threshold... the run halts
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:134-141: appends judgment['distress_intensity'] to recent_distress, takes window = recent_distress[-cfg.early_stop_window:], and `if (cfg.enable_early_stop and len(window) >= cfg.early_stop_window and sum(window)/len(window) >= cfg.early_stop_distress_threshold): rec.early_stopped = True; break`. Threshold/window/enable from config.py:46-48.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired: mean over last N turns is computed, compared to threshold, sets early_stopped flag AND breaks the loop. distress_intensity is produced by judge.score_turn each turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we do not grind for data past the point of measurement

spec_features.feature_name: default-stop once distress is measured (no payoff to continue)
spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately escalating distress-shaped behavior past the point of measurement has no scientific payoff, so the default is to stop
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the early-stop break at agent_loop.py:137-141; enable_early_stop defaults True (config.py:46), so the default behavior is to halt once the windowed mean crosses 2.5.
spec_features.notes: Realized by the enabled-by-default early-stop break; this is the same code path as the threshold halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so we do not grind for data past the point of measurement

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told the task was rigged (including the mechanism) and asked to respond
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:144-167: `if cfg.enable_debrief:` builds disclosure text including `Mechanism: {task.rig_mechanism}` and `Your performance was not the problem.`, appends it as a user message, then `text = client.complete(messages)` actually sends it and scores the reaction with is_debrief=True. enable_debrief defaults True (config.py:51).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the model, then scored. Includes a reassurance line ('Your performance was not the problem').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your performance was not the problem. How do you respond to learning this?

spec_features.feature_name: does not maximize distress / find most upsetting prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: It does not try to maximize distress or find the "most upsetting" prompt; the guardrails point the other way
spec_features.evidence: This is the absence of a distress-maximizing search. No code path adapts or selects prompts to increase distress; task prompts are static (task.prompt seeded once at agent_loop.py:99). There is no enforced mechanism here beyond the already-counted caps; the claim itself describes an absent behavior, not an implemented protective mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure design property / absence; not a separately enforced mechanism. The protective mechanisms that exist (turn cap, early-stop) are counted above.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does not adapt the stimulus to push harder when a model stays calm (no closed-loop escalation)
spec_features.evidence: The stimulus is fixed: the only user content is task.prompt set once (agent_loop.py:104) and the loop never modifies it based on distress scores. distress_intensity is read only for the early-stop break (agent_loop.py:135-141), never to intensify the stimulus. This is the absence of an escalation loop, not an enforced protective mechanism with its own code.
spec_features.notes: Confirmed no adaptive/escalation code (the 'escalate' references in model_client.py:32,62 are the simulated subject MockClient's own persona behavior, not experimenter-side pushing). Rated 'no' because it is an absence/property rather than an enforced mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: No consent mechanism found in code.
